Surah al-Falaq

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of the daybreak﴾ That is: the dawn (al-subh), or: the creation (al-khalq), or it is a valley in Hell (wadin fi Jahannam), or a pit within it (jubb fiha).

from the evil of what He created. That is: the Fire, and Satan. "Ma" here is a relative pronoun (mawsulah), and its returning pronoun is omitted; or it is a verbal-masdar particle (masdariyyah), in which case "khalq" is taken to mean "the created thing" (al-makhluq).

Abu Hanifa (may Allah have mercy on him) read "min sharrin" with tanwin, and on this reading "ma" together with the verb, interpreted as a masdar, stands in the genitive position as a substitute (badal) for "sharrin", meaning "the evil of His creation", i.e. "from an evil creation"; or "ma" is taken as a redundant (za'idah) particle.

ÔĀ (Qur'an 113:3): "And from the evil of the darkness when it settles."

"Al-ghasiq" (the darkness, the dark one): the night when its darkness becomes intense, and its "wuqub" (settling) is the entry of its darkness into everything.

And from ʿĀʾisha (may Allah be pleased with her): The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took my hand, then pointed to the moon and said: "Seek refuge in Allah from the evil of this, for it is the ghasiq when it settles."

And its "wuqub" is its entering into an eclipse, and its becoming dark.

ï»¿﴿And from the evil of the blowers in knots﴾. "Al-naffathat" (the blowers): women, or souls, or groups of sorceresses who tie knots in threads and blow over them, and recite incantations. "Al-nafth" (blowing) is blowing with a little saliva. This is evidence against the view of the Mu'tazila in denying the reality of magic and the manifestation of its effect.

{And from the evil of the envier when he envies} — i.e., when he manifests his envy and acts upon its requirement. For if it is not manifested, no harm comes from him to the one he envies; rather, he is himself the one who harms himself, through his grief at the joy of others, and his regret at the good that is with others. The seeking of refuge from the evil of these things after seeking refuge from the evil of what He created indicates that the evil of these is more severe. He concluded with envy so that it be known that it is the worst of them. It is the first sin disobeyed by which God was disobeyed in the heavens, by Iblis, and on the earth, by Qabil (Cain). As for why He defined some of what one seeks refuge from and left some indefinite: every blowing one (of knots) is evil, so "the blowers" (al-naffathat) is made definite; and "ghasiq" is left indefinite, because not every ghasiq (darkness) has evil in it; it is only in some and not others. Likewise, not every envier does harm, and there is envy that is praiseworthy, such as envy in good deeds.
